correctness.rationale: Unit-edge simplex has source-to-opposite-facet altitude H²=(n+1)/(2n), facet altitude h_f²=n/(2(n-1)), inradius r_f²=1/(2n(n-1)), and R=h_f+r_f. Unfold each adjacent facet across opposite ridge to a source at G-Ru_i; its straight path to p∈F crosses that ridge inside its convex hull and folds to an admissible two-facet path. Hence d²<=R²+|p-G|²+2R min_i<p-G,u_i><=R²+|p-G|², strictly away from G because facet normals span and sum zero. Ambient chord squared is H²+|p-G|², giving sharp constant sqrt((n+1)/(n-1)). For G, every path first enters opposite F at boundary q with |q-G|>=r_f, so its length >=sqrt(H²+r_f²)+r_f=R; path via ridge centroid attains R. Points in source-incident facets have intrinsic distance equal Euclidean chord. Direct verification of proof and pinned verifier, independent canonical-coordinate unfoldings for n=2,3,5,10,20 and 500 barycentric points. Finite samples corroborate rather than prove all dimensions.
